Planning for place: Place attachment and the founding of rural community
land trusts
Tom Moore
Department of Geography & Planning, University of Liverpool, United Kingdom
A R T I C L E I N F O A B S T R A C T
Keywords: This paper explores the role of place attachment in motivating residents of rural communities to form community
Community-led housing land trusts (CLTs). CLTs are non-profit community-led organisations formed and managed by volunteers. Their
Rural housing objectives typically relate to the provision of affordable housing. Using qualitative interview data collected from
Community land trusts
8 CLTs in rural England, this paper highlights the ways in which their founding members mobilise place at-
Place attachment
tachments to form CLTs, define and target beneficiaries, and acquire resources to facilitate affordable housing

Community planning

whilst challenging conventional logics of market housing provision. While CLT objectives are explicitly derived
from a desire to maintain, protect and enhance social and functional bonds to place, strong emphases on place
attachment in the planning and allocation of rural housing may deny housing opportunities to those without such
attachments.
